title: MINOR: Write the streams topology tombstone before the group epoch tombstone
body:
Deleting a streams group leaks its topics in the group coordinator's
topic-to-groups index (`groupsByTopics`), which `onMetadataUpdate` uses
to tell groups that a topic they depend on changed.

A streams group's entry in that index is derived from its topology:
replaying a `StreamsGroupTopologyValue` record subscribes the group to
the topology's required topics and replaying its tombstone unsubscribes
it. `StreamsGroup.createGroupTombstoneRecords` wrote the
`StreamsGroupMetadataValue` tombstone before the
`StreamsGroupTopologyValue` tombstone. On replay, the first one removes
the group, so the second one finds no group and returns before
unsubscribing anything. The entry survives for the lifetime of the
coordinator, and every deleted streams group adds to it. The consumer of
the index checks that the group still exists, so the effect is bounded
growth of the index and a spurious metadata refresh request on a group
that later reuses the id, not a failure.

This change writes the topology tombstone before the group epoch
tombstone. This restores the invariant the other group types already
have: every sibling record is torn down before the epoch tombstone, so
the epoch tombstone is the last record of a deletion. Deletions already
in the log with the previous order keep leaking on replay until
compaction removes their tombstones.

The new test builds a streams group with a topology, replays exactly the
records that `createGroupTombstoneRecords` produces, and verifies that
the group is removed and that the index no longer references it. It
fails with the previous record order.

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>
